inventory.item: A share is a slice of a business; 1 cr of 10 cr shares = 10%
Ramu Chai: 10 cr shares, profit 50, 5 cr profit behind each crore of shares
Market cap = price x shares; 100x10cr=1000cr; 50x20cr same
Price moves day to day without the business changing
Sales 500 -> costs and tax 440 (net of other income 4), interest 10, PAT 50
Value follows profit over years; price noisy over a day (zoom 1 day to 10 years)
Market cap sliders: price, shares; defaults 100, 10 cr, 1000 cr
TCPL share count 989,561,780 at Re 1; paid-up 98.96 cr
TCPL consolidated revenue 20,290.43; profit for year 1,546.80; owners 1,542.30; NCI 4.50
Hand-off to Part 2; later parts named (3, 7, 21)

assumptions: value per share grows at the profit-growth rate (constant multiple)
price = value x exp(gap); gap is a seeded mean-reverting random walk, ~1.2%/day, half-life ~1 yr, forced to today's slider price
lab.independent_calculation_method: Python 3.12 re-implementation of the seeded RNG, the price path and the ledger numbers, compared with window.labResults read from the page in headless Chromium (labtest.py, scratchpad)
lab.observed: 40 cases, 0 mismatches, max relative error 0 on market cap, value per share, value at window start/end, price at window start/end, price low/high, price-vs-value gap; price today == slider in all cases; ledger market-cap line matches; 0 JS errors
lab.hand_check: default 1-year window: value start = 100/1.12 = 89.2857; market cap 100x10 = 1000
lab.axis_and_clipping: x ticks at -T, -T/2, 0 via one scale function, tick text = labConfig.format; y auto-fit with 8% padding, floored at 0; nothing clipped
